candidate.answerReason: The principal square root of a² is |a|, which equals -a when a < 0.

methods.label: Use absolute value
methods.explanation: \(\sqrt{a^2}=|a|\). When \(a<0\), \(|a|=-a\), so the result is \(-a\) (which is positive).
methods.levelReason: The square-root identity and simplification of the absolute value of a negative number are within Grade 7.

methods.label: Use the principal-root definition
methods.explanation: Since \(a<0\), the number \(-a\) is positive and satisfies \((-a)^2=a^2\). The principal square root is the nonnegative square root, so \(\sqrt{a^2}=-a\), choice A.
methods.levelReason: This route uses the definition of the principal square root and elementary squaring, without requiring absolute-value notation.
